findings.finding: All 64 Python inputs were hashed and AST-parsed. The diagnostic searched 11,369 string occurrences / 6,281 unique constant values of at least five characters across all 62 actual pre/post Rust files. It reported 38 occurrences for 14 values; a raw hit is not a failed QA case.

Every one of the 38 hits was classified against its actual use. 13 are synthetic caller output; 8 are replacement/injected output; 2 are classification prefixes; 8 target sources outside the complete fmt transition; the remaining 7 compose actual source markers, covered by 12 targeted before/after span checks. No actual targeted marker count changed.

Selection/NextUse complete predecessor-read markers remain once before journal read and twice in the original finish path. The existing C whitespace-compaction matcher remains the actual matcher; it was not replaced with a looser rule.

The actual Legacy selection branch remains unique and contains exactly one snapshot/training, live, and trainer field occurrence each. Artifact read-order composite remains one exact match before/after. No deletion, replacement, attack assertion or matching rule is proposed here.

All 83 contract attack specifications retain their original unique-function and whitespace-token marker occurrence counts in actual pre/post source. This is an anchor diagnostic; no mutant was executed or rejected by this review.
All 17 ORDINARY_LITERAL_SPECS source paths are outside the 62 actual formatting changes. There is no formatter-based reason to change those strict prefixes, literal values or owner scopes.

Provider contract has 41 paths / 264 scope entries. The 26 paths touched by fmt contain 145 entries. Ordinary contract has 20 paths / 34 entries; 5 fmt-touched paths contain 8 entries. These are affected-path upper bounds; they do not mean all 145 or 8 hashes differ. The sole author recomputes exact changes from actual bytes.

Two ordinary mount parent paths changed bytes, but the native fmt semantic review retained the actual path attributes/module items. Parent-body hash refresh must preserve module identity, test guards, same-function boundaries and all previous forbidden/top-level/literal-call rules.

The exact provider contract hash is currently 2d2bc6b502d70b72ac07b27d6132bade55cf5874923c800ad33e24de993131d1. Its QA import check must follow the final refreshed contract bytes. Whole boundary count/digests must follow final registry bytes; original ORDINARY_NEW_BOUNDARIES [541:569] remains the same 28-item historical slice, while the provider extension is [569:].

The separate coordinator layer requires its exact new boundary/caller registration, Root FQNs and mount inventories. Append-only new entries must not turn ignored cases into default passes or change original stage budgets. This review does not approve the moving registration draft or projected counts.
